thesis.company_overview:
SK Telecom Co., Ltd. (SKM) is the U.S.-listed sponsored ADR of a South Korean communications operator that owns the network layer of the telecom value chain: it builds and operates wireless and fixed infrastructure and monetizes it through subscription connectivity and bundled services. Demand is driven by subscriber base, pricing/ARPU and data consumption, with sector economics defined by high fixed-cost network intensity, regulated pricing and long-lived capital commitments rather than cyclical volume swings. A segment revenue breakdown was not available for this issuer; see the latest annual report for business-line detail. A geographic revenue split was likewise not sourceable and is not stated here; the issuer is domiciled in South Korea per the market profile.

What the run does quantify is the valuation consequence of that model: the single DCF method returned a $65.70–$98.55 implied range against a $34.42 market price, i.e., the equity trades below the model's entire published band of $61.59–$102.65. The durable moat is structural rather than growth-driven — a nationwide network footprint and spectrum position create replicable-cost barriers, subscriber switching costs and interconnection scale economies, and the model capitalizes that durability with a 3.00% perpetuity growth rate after a 10-year forecast window. Institutional sponsorship on file is thin: 13F holders cover only 6.8% of shares outstanding, which limits visibility into holder concentration. The investment case therefore rests less on a fresh demand cycle than on a discount-rate and under-ownership gap that the DCF frames as material.

thesis.narrative:
SKM is a directional BUY with the point target deliberately withheld. The only valuation method that ran — a 10-year DCF at a 5.91% WACC and a 3.00% terminal growth rate — produced a $65.70 / $82.12 / $98.55 range, and the published ±25% band of $61.59–$102.65 sits entirely above the $34.42 market price. But a single method landing at 2.4x spot falls outside the [0.5x, 2x] calibration band, so the pipeline refuses to stamp a point on it; the direction, not a level, is the deliverable, and confidence is very_low.

The reverse-DCF explains the gap and is the crux of the call. Holding the model's growth fade fixed, $34.42 implies a 9.19% discount rate versus the model's 5.91% WACC; holding the WACC fixed, spot implies -8.35%/yr revenue growth held constant for 10 years, against the model's own fade averaging -0.4%/yr across the 10 forecast fiscal years. A flat rate and a declining fade schedule are different constructs, so the two are not directly comparable — but the market's single-variable solve is plainly more punitive on cash flows than the model, and that is where the directional upside sits.

Momentum supports rather than contradicts the call: the shares have returned +66.4% over the trailing year while sitting at 55% of their 52-week range, still 26.4% below the 52-week high. Sponsorship is thin — the 13F rows on file cover only 6.8% of shares outstanding — so the equity remains under-owned relative to the re-rating already underway. With no peer comp set available in this run, the valuation argument rests on the DCF band and the reverse-DCF read alone; that is a genuine evidentiary limitation and the reason the call carries very_low confidence.

Growth risk: the market's flat-rate solve of -8.35%/yr over the 10-year horizon is far harsher than the model's -0.4%/yr average fiscal-year fade; if the revenue decline proves structural rather than a mild fade, the valuation gap closes the wrong way.

thesis.valuation_overview:
Only one valuation method was run for SKM — a 10-year DCF at a 5.91% WACC, a -0.4%/yr average fiscal-year revenue fade and a 3.00% perpetuity — so there is no comps or DDM cross-check to triangulate against, and the peer screen returned no usable comp set for this ticker in this run. The DCF stands alone at $65.70 / $82.12 / $98.55 (low/mid/high).

Because that single method lands at $82.12, 2.4x the $34.42 market price, it falls outside the [0.5x, 2x] single-method calibration band; the pipeline therefore withholds the point target rather than stamping false precision on a lone, far-from-market output, leaving confidence at very_low. What survives is the ±25% confidence band of $61.59–$102.65, which sits entirely above the current price and frames direction, not a level.

The model-versus-market divergence is explained by the reverse-DCF: holding the model's fade fixed, $34.42 implies a 9.19% discount rate versus the model's 5.91%; holding the WACC fixed, spot implies -8.35%/yr revenue growth held constant for 10 years. Those are separate single-variable solves, not a joint forecast — so the band, not a point, is the honest output.
